questions.subject: mathematics
questions.text: If 3x + 5 = 20, what is the value of x?
questions.explanation: Subtract 5 from both sides to get 3x = 15, then divide both sides by 3. Therefore, x = 5.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.text: Factorise x² - 7x + 12.
questions.explanation: We need two numbers whose product is 12 and whose sum is -7. Those numbers are -3 and -4, giving (x - 3)(x - 4).

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.text: The sum of the roots of 2x² - 8x + 3 = 0 is:
questions.explanation: For ax² + bx + c = 0, the sum of the roots is -b/a. Here it is -(-8)/2 = 4.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.text: If y varies directly as x and y = 18 when x = 6, find y when x = 11.
questions.explanation: Direct variation gives y = kx. Since 18 = 6k, k = 3. When x = 11, y = 3 × 11 = 33.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.text: Solve simultaneously: x + y = 9 and x - y = 3.
questions.explanation: Add the equations to get 2x = 12, so x = 6. Substituting into x + y = 9 gives y = 3.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.text: Evaluate 2³ × 2⁴.
questions.explanation: When multiplying powers with the same base, add their indices: 2³ × 2⁴ = 2³⁺⁴ = 2⁷.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.text: Express 0.00056 in standard form.
questions.explanation: Move the decimal four places to the right to obtain 5.6, so the power is -4: 5.6 × 10⁻⁴.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.text: If log₂ 32 = n, find n.
questions.explanation: The statement asks for the power to which 2 must be raised to give 32. Since 2⁵ = 32, n = 5.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.text: Find the highest common factor of 36, 48 and 60.
questions.explanation: The common factors include 1, 2, 3, 4, 6 and 12. The greatest of these is 12.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.text: A trader increases a price of ₦8,000 by 15%. What is the new price?
questions.explanation: 15% of ₦8,000 is ₦1,200. Adding the increase gives ₦9,200.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.text: The angles of a triangle are 2x, 3x and 4x. Find x.
questions.explanation: Angles in a triangle sum to 180°. Thus 2x + 3x + 4x = 9x = 180°, so x = 20°.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.text: Find the area of a circle of radius 7 cm, taking π = 22/7.
questions.explanation: Area = πr² = 22/7 × 7 × 7 = 154 cm².

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.text: A right-angled triangle has shorter sides of 6 cm and 8 cm. Find its hypotenuse.
questions.explanation: By Pythagoras, c² = 6² + 8² = 36 + 64 = 100. Therefore c = 10 cm.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.text: The volume of a cuboid measuring 8 cm by 5 cm by 3 cm is:
questions.explanation: Volume of a cuboid is length × width × height: 8 × 5 × 3 = 120 cm³.

questions.subject: biology
questions.text: Which organelle releases energy from food during aerobic respiration?
questions.explanation: Mitochondria are the main sites of aerobic respiration and ATP production in eukaryotic cells.

questions.subject: biology
questions.text: The structure that controls movement of substances into and out of a cell is the:
questions.explanation: The cell membrane is selectively permeable and regulates movement between the cell and its surroundings.

questions.subject: biology
questions.text: Osmosis is the movement of water molecules from:
options: A concentrated solution to a dilute solution through any membrane
A dilute solution to a concentrated solution through a selectively permeable membrane
Low pressure to high pressure without a membrane
A concentrated solution to a dilute solution through a cell wall
questions.explanation: Osmosis is the net movement of water from higher water potential, usually a dilute solution, to lower water potential through a selectively permeable membrane.

questions.subject: biology
questions.text: Which structure is present in plant cells but absent from animal cells?
questions.explanation: Plant cells possess a rigid cellulose cell wall outside the cell membrane. Animal cells do not.

questions.subject: biology
questions.text: A gene expressed in a heterozygous individual is described as:
questions.explanation: A dominant allele produces its observable effect even when only one copy is present in a heterozygous individual.

questions.subject: biology
questions.text: In a cross Aa × Aa, what proportion of offspring is expected to be aa?
questions.explanation: The possible genotypes are AA, Aa, Aa and aa. One out of four is homozygous recessive, so the proportion is 1/4.

questions.subject: biology
questions.text: Variation caused by differences in genes is called:
questions.explanation: Genetic variation results from inherited differences in alleles, mutation and recombination.

questions.subject: biology
questions.text: Natural selection is most directly associated with the work of:
questions.explanation: Charles Darwin developed the theory of evolution by natural selection, independently paralleled by Alfred Russel Wallace.

questions.subject: biology
questions.text: An organism that feeds directly on a producer is a:
questions.explanation: Primary consumers occupy the second trophic level and obtain energy by feeding on producers.

questions.subject: biology
questions.text: The relationship in which both organisms benefit is known as:
questions.explanation: In mutualism, both participating organisms obtain a benefit from the association.

questions.subject: biology
questions.text: Which process returns carbon dioxide to the atmosphere?
questions.explanation: Respiration releases carbon dioxide from organisms, while combustion releases carbon dioxide from carbon-containing fuels.

questions.subject: biology
questions.text: The maximum population an environment can support sustainably is its:
questions.explanation: Carrying capacity is the largest population that available resources and environmental conditions can sustain over time.

questions.subject: english
questions.text: Choose the word nearest in meaning to “meticulous”.
questions.explanation: Meticulous describes someone who pays close and careful attention to detail.

questions.subject: english
questions.text: Neither the principal nor the teachers ___ available.
questions.explanation: With neither...nor, the verb agrees with the nearer subject. “Teachers” is plural, so “were” is correct.

questions.subject: english
questions.text: If I ___ enough money, I would buy the books.
questions.explanation: This is a second conditional sentence describing an unreal present situation: if + past simple, followed by would + base verb.

questions.subject: english
questions.text: The committee has submitted ___ report.
questions.explanation: When treated as a single unit, the collective noun “committee” takes the singular possessive determiner “its”.

questions.subject: english
questions.text: Choose the correctly punctuated sentence.
questions.explanation: When “however” introduces the sentence as a conjunctive adverb, it is followed by a comma.

questions.subject: english
questions.text: The main function of a topic sentence is to:
options: Give every example in the paragraph
questions.explanation: A topic sentence states or signals the central idea that the supporting sentences develop.

questions.subject: english
questions.text: An inference is best described as:
options: A statement copied directly from a passage
A conclusion drawn from evidence in a passage
questions.explanation: An inference is a reasonable conclusion reached by combining textual evidence with what the reader already knows.

questions.subject: english
questions.text: A writer’s attitude toward a subject is referred to as the writer’s:
questions.explanation: Tone expresses the writer’s attitude or emotional stance toward the subject or audience.

questions.subject: english
questions.text: To read a passage quickly in order to identify its general idea is to:
questions.explanation: Skimming is rapid reading for the main idea. Scanning is rapid searching for a specific detail.

questions.subject: english
questions.text: Which word has the same vowel sound as “seat”?
questions.explanation: Both “seat” and “seize” contain the long /iː/ vowel sound.

questions.subject: english
questions.text: Which word has a different initial consonant sound?
questions.explanation: “Chemist,” “character” and “chorus” begin with /k/. “Church” begins with /tʃ/.

questions.subject: english
questions.text: In which word is the second syllable stressed?
questions.explanation: “Relax” is stressed on its second syllable: re-LAX. The other listed words are stressed on the first syllable.

questions.subject: english
questions.text: Which pair of words forms a minimal pair?
questions.explanation: “Ship” and “sheep” differ by only one phoneme, /ɪ/ versus /iː/, so they form a minimal pair.
